items.title: Tommy Newsom and Ross Tompkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: I made an album with her several years ago, with Monty Budwig and Jake Hanna.

ctx.x: Did you do something with Jane Jarvis fairly recently?

I made an album with her several years ago, with Monty Budwig and Jake Hanna. That was fun. And we did it in a little small studio. Yeah I’d forgotten about that, that was nice. Those things come and go, it’s hard to predict. I had forgotten about, from being steadily employed all those years, you know. But now you can’t predict what’s happening. I mean there’s things coming up, I’ve got something in Phoenix next year and something with Jane Jarvis in Tampa this year in November. But somehow it fills itself in,…

Yeah, I was looking the other day, because we worked every day for so long it was funny not to show up someplace every day, until you get used to it. And I’m looking, the only way I can keep track is the American Express book calendar they send you once a year and you can write down where you’re supposed to be. And as I looked through my book it’s slowly getting busier and busier. It’s slow but—

items.title: Jake Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: Ross Tompkins knows him. ... Ross Tompkins’ father knew him in Detroit. ... Ross Tompkins got it all down, you know. ... Ross Tompkins or Teddy Wilson would always ask if he could have me you know.

ctx.x: Okay? That you told to a very famous lady. You had three childhood heroes: Brace Beemer—
Brace Beemer, The Lone Ranger. Ross Tompkins knows him.
